review_notes: I read the whole file. It has one theorem and no simp attributes of its own. Its simp usage is two `simpa only` calls (`simpa only [F,L,hR] using he₁` and `simpa only [hw,haD] using ...`). I checked how `a.density` is exposed. `spectralContinuousCoefficient_density` is a `rfl` lemma in SpectralContinuousMultiplier.lean and is not tagged `@[simp]`. I grepped the same local `haD : a.density=radialMatchedFreeTransportFunction z := rfl` in four other Profile files, which suggests the missing interface is real. I did not run Lean, so I can't say whether adding `@[simp]` would also change other simp calls (for example, ones that unfold `a.density` through `simp only` or `simp`). That would need a check of downstream `simp` users. I found no loops or competing rules in this file.

findings.problem: The proof re-proves `a.density = radialMatchedFreeTransportFunction z` as a local `rfl` fact and passes it to `simpa only`. The general projection lemma `spectralContinuousCoefficient_density` already exists, but it is not marked `@[simp]`, so simp cannot rewrite `(spectralContinuousCoefficient R q hq).density` to `q` by default. The same local `haD := rfl` appears in RadialMatchedWeakExterior, RadialMatchedWeakChainExterior and RadialMatchedPencilRobin, so each use site repeats the workaround. Because `a` is a `let`, the local fact is also tied to this particular `a` instead of the general constructor.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `spectralContinuousCoefficient_density` in SpectralContinuousMultiplier.lean as `@[simp]`. Its left side is a projection of a constructor-like definition and its right side is a strictly simpler variable, so it cannot loop. Then drop `haD` here and in the other three files, and call `simpa only [hw, spectralContinuousCoefficient_density]` (or plain `simp [hw]`). Alternatively, keep a single non-simp specialised lemma `(spectralContinuousCoefficient R (radialMatchedFreeTransportFunction z) h).density = radialMatchedFreeTransportFunction z` for these Profile files.
findings.benefit: The density projection gets one canonical normal form, so profile proofs no longer restate the same `rfl` fact and the repeated boilerplate goes away. Readers can see which rewrite is used.
